title: handoff
universal_lens: The system enforces a strict, append-only temporal evolution of state. Transitions are governed by immutable phase boundaries and isolated branching topologies, ensuring that the foundational algebraic structure remains invariant while higher-order functional layers are sequentially appended without retroactive mutation.
gsi_mapping: Treating each development phase as an independent conformal block, the read-only audit establishes a baseline predictive distribution. The strict prohibition on merging to main ensures zero posterior leakage between epochs, maintaining exact calibration integrity across the entire sequential inference pipeline.
gse_mapping: Operational states transition deterministically through isolated branches. The sandbox-side mirror acts as a frictionless simulation environment, decoupling execution dynamics from physical ACL constraints, thereby guaranteeing that state mutations remain strictly localized and reversible.

primitives.name: Append-Only Temporal Lock
primitives.verbatim_quote: > Each phase appends a new section; older sections are not edited after sign-off.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Phase index k (dimensionless integer), Sign-off time t_k (ISO 8601 timestamp).
primitives.assumptions: Time is strictly monotonic; once a phase reaches a terminal state (sign-off), its informational content becomes immutable.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Violated if any retroactive edit occurs to a signed-off section, collapsing the causal chain and invalidating historical baselines.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to the conservation of information in closed quantum systems; past states cannot be overwritten, only unitarily evolved forward.
layer2.telemetry: Git history diff checks against signed-off commit hashes.

primitives.name: Isolated Branch Topology
primitives.verbatim_quote: > Branch policy: one branch per phase, no merges to `main`, no PRs unless explicitly requested.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Branch set B = {b_1, ..., b_n} (topological nodes), Merge operator M (boolean flag).
primitives.assumptions: Branches operate as disjoint sets with respect to the primary integration trunk (`main`).
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down if unauthorized merges occur, causing state-space entanglement and cross-phase contamination.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's parallel universe simulation kernel, where distinct situational hypotheses are evaluated in isolation before explicit aggregation.
layer2.telemetry: CI/CD pipeline rejection logs for unauthorized merge attempts.

primitives.name: Sandbox Friction Decoupling
primitives.verbatim_quote: ### 1.3 Commands run & results All commands run from a sandbox-side mirror of the working tree at `/tmp/work/Sports` (npm install on the Windows-mounted folder is ~100× slower and `rm` is blocked by ACLs — see §1.7).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Execution time T_exec (seconds), ACL constraint C_acl (boolean), Mirror distance D_mirror (filesystem path length).
primitives.assumptions: A byte-identical mirror exists in a frictionless execution space (Linux sandbox) decoupled from host OS constraints.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails if the mirror diverges from the source tree or if sandbox permissions mimic host ACL blocks.

layer2.mapping: Mirrors GSI's technique of running heavy Monte Carlo simulations in decoupled compute clusters to avoid blocking the primary inference thread.
layer2.telemetry: Ratio of sandbox execution time vs. native mount execution time (~100x).

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: These primitives trace their lineage to early version control theory (RCS, CVS) and the mathematical formalization of persistent data structures. The append-only constraint mirrors the axioms of blockchain ledgers and immutable event sourcing, ensuring auditability. The isolation principle derives from modular programming paradigms and microkernel operating system designs, where fault containment is paramount. The sandboxing technique reflects the broader computational trend of containerization (Docker, chroot), isolating environmental variables to ensure reproducible scientific computation.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: The decision actors here are the quantitative researchers and DevOps engineers managing the GSI/GSE lifecycle. Their cognitive model prioritizes risk mitigation and reproducibility over raw velocity. By enforcing strict branch policies and sandboxed execution, they anticipate human error (accidental overwrites) and environmental instability (OS-level ACLs). They act as rational agents seeking to maximize the signal-to-noise ratio in their development pipeline, treating the codebase not just as executable instructions but as a curated, verifiable knowledge artifact.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A veto condition triggers if the sandbox mirror exhibits byte-level divergence from the canonical source tree, invalidating the friction-decoupling assumption. Similarly, if a phase attempts to modify a previously signed-off section, the append-only invariant is breached, necessitating an immediate halt to preserve historical integrity. Cross-layer leakage occurs if environment variables or database states from the sandbox inadvertently pollute the host machine's configuration, violating the strict isolation required for clean experimental replication.
